questions.title: Box Volume Constructor Choice
questions.description:
A packaging team uses two kinds of boxes: a standard test box that is always 1 x 1 x 1, and custom boxes whose dimensions come from the order sheet. Define a class Box with a default (no-argument) constructor that sets length, width and height all to 1, and a parameterized constructor Box(int length, int width, int height). The input decides which constructor to use: the token D builds the standard default box, the token P builds a custom box from the next three numbers. Print the box volume using a volume() method.

Input Format:
One line: either D, or P followed by three space-separated integers length width height.

Output Format:
One line: Volume: <volume>

Constraints:
mode is D or P; 1 <= length, width, height <= 1000
questions.inputconstrains: mode is D or P; 1 <= length, width, height <= 1000

questions.title: Student Constructor Display
questions.description:
The school office registers a new student by passing the name and roll number straight into a parameterized constructor. Define a class Student with fields name and roll and a constructor Student(String name, int roll) that stores both values. Add a display() method that prints the two fields. In main, read the values, create the object using the constructor, and call display().

Input Format:
One line: name roll (name is a single word, roll is an integer).

Output Format:
Line 1: Name: <name>
Line 2: Roll: <roll>

Constraints:
1 <= name length <= 20, 1 <= roll <= 9999

questions.title: Visitor Counter Default Start
questions.description:
A hall's visitor counter starts from a fixed base value that its no-argument constructor sets: 100 visitors were pre-registered. Define a class Counter with a default constructor that sets count to 100 and an increment() method that raises the count by 1. Read the number of walk-in visitors, create one Counter with the default constructor, call increment() that many times, and print the final count.

Input Format:
One integer: extraVisitors.

Output Format:
One line: Total: <final count>

Constraints:
0 <= extraVisitors <= 1000

questions.title: Book Copy by Constructor
questions.description:
A library app duplicates a Book record using a copy constructor. Define class Book with fields title and price, a parameterized constructor Book(String title, int price), and a copy constructor Book(Book other) that copies both fields from another book. Read title, price and extra. Create the original book with the parameterized constructor, create a duplicate with the copy constructor, add extra to the duplicate's price, then print both records.

Input Format:
One line: title price extra (title is a single word).

Output Format:
Line 1: Title: <original title>
Line 2: Price: <original price>
Line 3: Title: <duplicate title>
Line 4: Price: <duplicate price>

Constraints:
1 <= title length <= 20, 0 <= price <= 10000, 0 <= extra <= 1000

questions.title: Shadow Free Rectangle
questions.description:
When a constructor's parameter names are identical to the field names, the fields hide behind the parameters unless you use the this keyword. Define a class Rectangle with fields length and width and a constructor Rectangle(int length, int width) whose parameter names exactly match the field names; assign them using this.length and this.width. Read the two values, construct the rectangle, and print the area with an area() method.

Input Format:
One line: two space-separated integers length and width.

Output Format:
One line: Area: <length * width>

Constraints:
1 <= length, width <= 1000

questions.title: Clock Time Constructor
questions.description:
A digital clock receives raw hour and minute values from a sensor and must normalize them inside its parameterized constructor. Define a class Clock with fields hours and minutes and a constructor Clock(int h, int m) that stores h + m / 60 into hours and m % 60 into minutes, then wraps hours with % 24. Read h and m, construct the clock, and print the time as two digits for hours and two digits for minutes joined by a colon.

Input Format:
One line: two space-separated integers h and m.

Output Format:
One line: the normalized time in hh:mm form, e.g. 07:05

Constraints:
0 <= h <= 23, 0 <= m <= 180

questions.title: Pizza Order Constructor
questions.description:
A pizzeria's ordering kiosk builds a Pizza object for every customer. If the customer just picks the surprise option, the kiosk uses the default constructor, which always produces a Small pizza with Cheese. Otherwise the kiosk uses the parameterized constructor with the chosen size and topping. Define class Pizza with fields size and topping, a no-argument constructor that sets size to Small and topping to Cheese, and a parameterized constructor Pizza(String size, String topping). Read the mode token: D means use the default constructor, P means read two more words (size, topping) and use the parameterized constructor. Print the order.

Input Format:
One line: either D, or P followed by two space-separated words size and topping.

Output Format:
Line 1: Size: <size>
Line 2: Topping: <topping>

Constraints:
mode is D or P; size and topping are single words of length 1..15
questions.inputconstrains: mode is D or P; size and topping are single words of length 1..15

questions.title: Bank Account Opening Balance
questions.description:
Silverline Bank opens a savings account by feeding the holder's name and the opening balance into a parameterized constructor. As a launch offer, the constructor itself adds a welcome bonus of 200 to any opening balance of 5000 or more. Define class SavingsAccount with fields holder and balance and a constructor SavingsAccount(String holder, int balance) that stores the holder and the (possibly bonus-boosted) balance. Read the values, create the account, and print both fields.

Input Format:
One line: holder balance (holder is a single word, balance is an integer).

Output Format:
Line 1: Holder: <holder>
Line 2: Balance: <balance after any bonus>

Constraints:
1 <= holder length <= 20, 0 <= balance <= 100000

questions.title: Laptop Spec Card
questions.description:
A computer shop prints a spec card for every laptop on display. The showcase unit always uses the default constructor: model Generic with 4 GB RAM and 256 GB storage. Custom builds use the parameterized constructor. Define class Laptop with fields model, ram and storage, a no-argument constructor with the showcase defaults, and a parameterized constructor Laptop(String model, int ram, int storage). Read the mode token: B means default constructor, C means read a model word and two integers and use the parameterized constructor. Print the spec card.

Input Format:
One line: either B, or C followed by model ram storage.

Output Format:
Line 1: Model: <model>
Line 2: RAM: <ram>GB
Line 3: Storage: <storage>GB

Constraints:
mode is B or C; 1 <= model length <= 20, 1 <= ram <= 128, 1 <= storage <= 2048
questions.inputconstrains: mode is B or C; 1 <= model length <= 20, 1 <= ram <= 128, 1 <= storage <= 2048

questions.title: Temperature Sensor Copy
questions.description:
A weather station keeps a live Sensor reading and a backup copy created with a copy constructor. Calibration later shifts only the backup by an offset. Define class Sensor with field reading, a parameterized constructor Sensor(int reading), and a copy constructor Sensor(Sensor other) that copies the reading. Read the reading and the offset; create the live sensor, create the backup with the copy constructor, add the offset to the backup's reading, then print both.

Input Format:
One line: reading offset (both integers).

Output Format:
Line 1: Sensor: <live reading>
Line 2: Backup: <backup reading>

Constraints:
-50 <= reading <= 150, 0 <= offset <= 50

questions.title: Game Settings Default First
questions.description:
Every new game profile starts from a default settings object built by the no-argument constructor: difficulty Normal, sound on, volume 50. The player may then open the settings menu and update difficulty and volume through setter methods; sound can never be changed. Define class GameSettings with fields difficulty (String), sound (boolean) and volume (int), a no-argument constructor that sets the three defaults, methods setDifficulty(String d) and setVolume(int v), and a print() method. Read the mode token: DEFAULT means just create the object with the default constructor and print it; UPDATE means read a difficulty word and a volume and apply both setters before printing.

Input Format:
One line: either DEFAULT, or UPDATE followed by a difficulty word and an integer volume.

Output Format:
Line 1: Difficulty: <difficulty>
Line 2: Sound: on
Line 3: Volume: <volume>

Constraints:
mode is DEFAULT or UPDATE; difficulty is a single word of length 1..15, 0 <= volume <= 100
questions.inputconstrains: mode is DEFAULT or UPDATE; difficulty is a single word of length 1..15, 0 <= volume <= 100

questions.title: Ticket Category Constructor
questions.description:
A concert counter builds a Ticket object for every sale, and the parameterized constructor itself does all the pricing: a VIP ticket costs 250 and a Regular ticket costs 100, and the constructor computes total = unitPrice * quantity. Define class Ticket with fields category, quantity, unitPrice and total, and a constructor Ticket(String category, int quantity) that stores category and quantity, decides unitPrice from the category, and computes total. Read category and quantity, create the ticket, and print the stored values.

Input Format:
One line: category quantity (category is the word VIP or Regular).

Output Format:
Line 1: Category: <category>
Line 2: Tickets: <quantity>
Line 3: Total: <total>

Constraints:
category is VIP or Regular, 0 <= quantity <= 100
questions.inputconstrains: category is VIP or Regular, 0 <= quantity <= 100

questions.title: Box Arity Constructor Choice
questions.description:
A timber yard sizes boxes by how many measurements the clerk enters: one number means a cube (all three sides equal), two numbers mean a flat box of the given length and width with height fixed at 1. Define class Box with fields length, width, height, a constructor Box(int side) that sets all three fields to side, and an overloaded constructor Box(int length, int width) that stores the two values and sets height to 1. Read the whole input line and let the number of integers decide which constructor runs. Print the volume via a volume() method.

Input Format:
One line containing either one integer side, or two integers length width.

Output Format:
One line: Volume: <volume>

Constraints:
the line has 1 or 2 integers, each 1..1000
questions.inputconstrains: the line has 1 or 2 integers, each 1..1000

questions.title: Student Copy Independence
questions.description:
An exam cell keeps the original Student record untouched and works on a duplicate created with a copy constructor. Define class Student with fields name and marks, a parameterized constructor Student(String name, int marks), a copy constructor Student(Student other) that copies both fields, and a setMarks(int m) method. Read name, marks and newMarks; create the original, create a duplicate with the copy constructor, update only the duplicate's marks with setMarks, then print both records to prove the original never changed.

Input Format:
One line: name marks newMarks (name is a single word).

Output Format:
Line 1: Original: <name> <marks>
Line 2: Copy: <name> <newMarks>

Constraints:
1 <= name length <= 20, 0 <= marks <= 100, 0 <= newMarks <= 100

questions.title: Order Chain Constructor Print
questions.description:
A warehouse logs every order at creation time. Define class Order with fields id and city, a constructor Order(int id) that stores the id and prints Base: <id>, and an overloaded constructor Order(int id, String city) that chains to the one-argument constructor with this(id) before storing the city and printing City: <city>. Read the whole input line: one integer creates a base order, an integer followed by a city word creates a tagged order. The chained construction must print the base line first, then the city line.

Input Format:
One line: either one integer id, or id and a city word.

Output Format:
Line 1: Base: <id>
Line 2 (only when a city is given): City: <city>

Constraints:
1 <= id <= 99999; city is a single word of length 1..20
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= id <= 99999; city is a single word of length 1..20

questions.title: Employee Shadow Salary
questions.description:
Payroll wants the constructor parameters to carry the same names as the fields, so the this keyword is mandatory to reach the fields. Define class Employee with fields name and salary and a constructor Employee(String name, int salary) whose parameter names exactly match the fields; assign them via this.name and this.salary. Also write applyBonus(int bonus) that updates this.salary = this.salary + bonus. Read name, salary and bonus, construct the employee, apply the bonus, and print both fields.

Input Format:
One line: name salary bonus (name is a single word).

Output Format:
Line 1: Name: <name>
Line 2: Salary: <salary + bonus>

Constraints:
1 <= name length <= 20, 0 <= salary <= 100000, 0 <= bonus <= 1000

questions.title: Box Creation History Counter
questions.description:
A factory tracks how its boxes are built. Every Box constructor must count itself: the default constructor increments a static counter for default builds, the parameterized constructor increments a static counter for sized builds, and the copy constructor increments a static counter for copies. Define class Box with three static int counters (countDefault, countParam, countCopy) and field side. Box() sets side to 1 and counts as default; Box(int side) stores side and counts as parameterized; Box(Box other) copies the other box's side and counts as copy. Read the whole command line and process it left to right: D builds a default box, P followed by a number builds a parameterized box, C builds a copy of the most recently built box (the first command is always D or P, so a box to copy always exists). After all commands print the three counters.

Input Format:
One line of space-separated commands: D, P side, or C.

Output Format:
Line 1: Default: <countDefault>
Line 2: Parameterized: <countParam>
Line 3: Copy: <countCopy>

Constraints:
1 <= number of commands <= 100; the first command is D or P; 1 <= side <= 1000
questions.input3: P 2 D P 3 C C D
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= number of commands <= 100; the first command is D or P; 1 <= side <= 1000

questions.title: Money Copy Add Method
questions.description:
A wallet app models money with a class whose add operation never mutates its operands: Money add(Money other) builds the result as a copy of the current object using the copy constructor and then increases the copy by the other amount. Define class Money with field amount, a parameterized constructor Money(int amount), a copy constructor Money(Money other), and the add method as described (it returns a new Money). Read two amounts, build first and second, compute total = first.add(second), and print both operands and the total to show the operands were untouched.

Input Format:
One line: two space-separated integers.

Output Format:
Line 1: First: <first amount>
Line 2: Second: <second amount>
Line 3: Total: <sum>

Constraints:
0 <= amount <= 100000

questions.title: Logger Chain Trail
questions.description:
A monitoring tool records construction steps in a static trail string. Define class ChainLogger with a static String trail that starts empty. The base constructor ChainLogger() appends the letter B to the trail. The tagged constructor ChainLogger(String tag) first chains to the base constructor with this() (which appends B) and then appends the letter T itself. Read the whole command line and process it left to right: B constructs a base logger, T followed by a tag word constructs a tagged logger. Because of chaining, every tagged construction adds BOTH letters, B then T. Finally print the trail.

Input Format:
One line of space-separated commands: B, or T tag.

Output Format:
One line: the trail string made of the letters B and T in creation order.

Constraints:
1 <= number of commands <= 50; every T is followed by one tag word of length 1..20
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= number of commands <= 50; every T is followed by one tag word of length 1..20

questions.title: Product Catalog Constructor Fit
questions.description:
A stockroom builds its catalog by handing each item to the smallest constructor that fits the data given: a bare name uses Product(String name) leaving price and qty at 0, a name with a price uses Product(String name, int price) leaving qty at 0, and a name with price and quantity uses Product(String name, int price, int qty). Define class Product with fields name, price, qty and these three overloaded constructors. Read n, then read n item lines (each with 1, 2 or 3 space-separated values) and build each product with the fitting constructor. Finally print every item.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: a name, or name price, or name price qty.

Output Format:
n lines, one per product: Item: <name>, Price: <price>, Qty: <qty>

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100; 1 <= name length <= 20; 0 <= price <= 10000; 0 <= qty <= 1000
